title: "Inter-VLAN Routing and DHCP"

# Inter-VLAN Routing and DHCP

The VLAN lab stopped at layer 2. This one adds switched virtual interfaces so VLAN 10 can reach VLAN 20, then turns the same switch into the DHCP server for VLAN 10.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Route between two VLANs on one cEOS switch
- Point a host default at the SVI
- Serve DHCP for one VLAN from EOS
- See that a host with no route still cannot leave its subnet

## Topology

One cEOS switch and three Alpine hosts. h1 and h3 are VLAN 10. h2 is VLAN 20. h3 starts with no address and asks DHCP.

```yaml
name: svi
topology:
  kinds:
    arista_ceos:
      image: ceos:4.37.0F
      memory: 2G
  nodes:
    sw:
      kind: arista_ceos
    h1:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - ip addr add 172.16.10.11/24 dev eth1
        - ip link set eth1 up
        - ip route add default via 172.16.10.1
    h2:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - ip addr add 172.16.20.11/24 dev eth1
        - ip link set eth1 up
        - ip route add default via 172.16.20.1
    h3:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - ip link set eth1 up
  links:
    - endpoints: ["h1:eth1", "sw:eth1"]
    - endpoints: ["h2:eth1", "sw:eth2"]
    - endpoints: ["h3:eth1", "sw:eth3"]
```

## Switch

```text
vlan 10
   name users
vlan 20
   name servers
interface Ethernet1
   switchport access vlan 10
interface Ethernet2
   switchport access vlan 20
interface Ethernet3
   switchport access vlan 10
interface Vlan10
   ip address 172.16.10.1/24
interface Vlan20
   ip address 172.16.20.1/24
ip routing
ip dhcp server
ip dhcp pool USERS
   network 172.16.10.0/24
   range 172.16.10.50 172.16.10.80
   default-gateway 172.16.10.1
   lease 0 0 10
```

`ip routing` is required. Without it the SVIs exist and do not forward.

On h3, after the switch is configured:

```bash
docker exec clab-svi-h3 udhcpc -i eth1 -n -q
docker exec clab-svi-h3 ip addr show eth1
```

## Verify

```bash
docker exec clab-svi-h1 ping -c 2 172.16.20.11
docker exec clab-svi-sw Cli -c "show ip route"
docker exec clab-svi-sw Cli -c "show ip dhcp binding"
```

### Predict

- h1 reaches h2 through the switch. The first hop is 172.16.10.1.
- h3 has an address inside 172.16.10.50–80 and a default route.
- Remove `ip routing`. The SVIs stay up and the ping between VLANs fails. Put it back.

## Drill

Add a static host route nowhere: on h1, `ip route del default`. The ping to h2 fails. The ping to 172.16.10.12, if you give h3 a moment, still works if you ping inside the VLAN. Restore the default.
